arxiv-2012-13614.title: Quantile regression with generated dependent variable and covariates
arxiv-2012-13614.creator: Jayeeta Bhattacharya
arxiv-2012-13614.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Jayeeta Bhattacharya. We study linear quantile regression models when regressors and/or dependent variable are not directly observed but estimated in an initial first step and used in the second step quantile regression for estimating the quantile parameters. This general class of generated quantile regression (GQR) covers various statistical applications, for instance, estimation of endogenous quantile regression models and triangular structural equation models, and some new relevant applications are discussed.

arxiv-2104-14220.title: Emission lines from X-ray illuminated accretion disc in black hole binaries 2020 Emission lines from X-ray illuminated accretion disc in black hole binaries – References
arxiv-2104-14220.creator: Santanu Mondal, Tek P. Adhikari, Chandra B. Singh
arxiv-2104-14220.description: Abstract X-ray flux from the inner hot region around central compact object in a binary system illuminates the upper surface of an accretion disc and it behaves like a corona. This region can be photoionised by the illuminating radiation, thus can emit different emission lines.

arxiv-2205-08366.title: A Deep-learning Model for Fast Prediction of Vacancy Formation in Diverse Materials
arxiv-2205-08366.creator: Kamal Choudhary, Bobby G. Sumpter
arxiv-2205-08366.description: Abstract The presence of point defects such as vacancies plays an important role in material design. Here, we demonstrate that a graph neural network (GNN) model trained only on perfect materials can also be used to predict vacancy formation energies ( E v ​ a ​ c E_{vac} ) of defect structures without the need for additional training data.

arxiv-2211-01344.title: A New Test for Market Efficiency and Uncovered Interest Parity
arxiv-2211-01344.creator: Richard T. Baillie
arxiv-2211-01344.description: Abstract First Draft: September 26, 2021 This Draft: August 8, 2026 Abstract: We suggest a new single-equation test for Uncovered Interest Parity ( UIP ) based on a dynamic regression approach. The method provides consistent and asymptotically efficient parameter estimates, and is not dependent on assumptions of strict exogeneity.

arxiv-2211-09946.title: Inertial Force Transmission in Dense Granular Flows
arxiv-2211-09946.creator: Matthew Macaulay, Pierre Rognon
arxiv-2211-09946.description: Abstract Dense granular flows are well described by several continuum models, however, their internal dynamics remain elusive. This study explores the contact force distributions in simulated steady and homogenous shear flows. Results demonstrate the existence of high magnitude contact forces in faster flows with stiffer grains. A proposed physical mechanism explains this rate-dependent force transmission.

arxiv-2403-02993.title: Localized Zeroth-Order Prompt Optimization
arxiv-2403-02993.creator: Wenyang Hu, Yao Shu, Zongmin Yu, Zhaoxuan Wu, Xiaoqiang Lin, Zhongxiang Dai, See-Kiong Ng, & Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
arxiv-2403-02993.description: Abstract The efficacy of large language models (LLMs) in understanding and generating natural language has aroused a wide interest in developing prompt-based methods to harness the power of black-box LLMs. Existing methodologies usually prioritize a global optimization for finding the global optimum, which however will perform poorly in certain tasks.

arxiv-2404-03324.title: A Comparative Analysis of Word-Level Metric Differential Privacy: Benchmarking The Privacy-Utility Trade-off
arxiv-2404-03324.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . The application of Differential Privacy to Natural Language Processing techniques has emerged in relevance in recent years, with an increasing number of studies published in established NLP outlets. In particular, the adaptation of Differential Privacy for use in NLP tasks has first focused on the word-level , where calibrated noise is added to word embedding vectors to achieve “noisy” representations. To this end, several implementations have appeared in the literature, each presenting an alternative method of achieving word-level Differential Privacy.

arxiv-2405-18541.title: Low-Rank Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2405-18541.creator: Maxime Zanella, UMons, Ismail Ben Ayed, code: https://github.com/MaxZanella/CLIP-LoRA
arxiv-2405-18541.description: Abstract Recent progress in the few-shot adaptation of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) has further pushed their generalization capabilities, at the expense of just a few labeled samples within the target downstream task. However, this promising, already quite abundant few-shot literature has focused principally on prompt learning and, to a lesser extent, on adapters, overlooking the recent advances in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT).

arxiv-2410-03415.title: Surgical, Cheap, and Flexible: Mitigating False Refusal in Language Models via Single Vector Ablation
arxiv-2410-03415.creator: Xinpeng Wang, Chengzhi Hu, Paul Röttger, Barbara Plank
arxiv-2410-03415.description: Abstract Training a language model to be both helpful and harmless requires careful calibration of refusal behaviours: Models should refuse to follow malicious instructions or give harmful advice (e.g. “how do I kill someone?”), but they should not refuse safe requests, even if they superficially resemble unsafe ones (e.g. “how do I kill a Python process?”).

arxiv-2502-06144.title: On finite approximations of transitive graphs
arxiv-2502-06144.creator: Andreas Thom
arxiv-2502-06144.description: Abstract . In this note we answer a question of Johannes Carmesin, which was circulated at the Oberwolfach Workshop on ”Graph Theory” in January 2025. We provide a unimodular, locally finite, and vertex-transitive graph without any perfect finite r r -local model for r ∈ ℕ r\in\mathbb{N} large enough.

arxiv-2504-20883.title: Guessing Efficiently for Constrained Subspace Approximation
arxiv-2504-20883.creator: Adita Bhaskara, Sepideh Mahabadi, Madhusudhan Reddy Pittu, Ali Vakilian, David P. Woodruff
arxiv-2504-20883.description: Abstract In this paper we study constrained subspace approximation problem. Given a set of n n points { a 1 , … , a n } \{a_{1},\ldots,a_{n}\} in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , the goal of the subspace approximation problem is to find a k k dimensional subspace that best approximates the input points.

britannica-1911-false-pretences.title: False Pretences (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-false-pretences.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-false-pretences.description: Article 'False Pretences' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. other person by any false pretence any chattel, money or valuable security, with intent to defraud. It is an indictable misdemeanour under the Larceny Act of 1861. The broad distinction between this offence and larceny is that in the former the owner intends to part with his property, in the latter he does not. This offence dates as a statutory crime practically from 1756.

pmc-10480691.title: Sprinting with bilateral transtibial running-specific prostheses versus biological limbs – are they comparable? Comments on Beck et al. (2022)
pmc-10480691.creator: M J Connick, E M Beckman, S M Tweedy
pmc-10480691.description: Since publication of this paper (Royal Society open science, 2022. 9(1): p. 211799), the authors have published a correction clarifying that the paper presents a case study that ‘… did not meet the definition for research with regard to human subjects'. The data are incorrectly referred to as experimental because the study has no experimental control.

pmc-10495338.title: Oit3, a promising hallmark gene for targeting liver sinusoidal endothelial cells
pmc-10495338.creator: Zhi-Wen Li, Bai Ruan, Pei-Jun Yang, Jing-Jing Liu, Ping Song, Juan-Li Duan, Lin Wang
pmc-10495338.description: Liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) play a pivotal role in maintaining liver homeostasis and influencing the pathological processes of various liver diseases. However, neither LSEC-specific hallmark genes nor a LSEC promoter-driven Cre mouse line has been introduced before, which largely restricts the study of liver diseases with vascular disorders.

pmc-10514763.creator: Rachel S Goodman, Lavanya Mittal, Eva Rawlings Parker, Robert Dellavalle, Darlinton Carvalho, Tianyu Dong
pmc-10514763.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundEnvironmental vinyl chloride (VC) exposure may result in serious acute and chronic dermatological conditions. pmc-10566296.title: Effectiveness and safety of pelareorep plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone for advanced solid tumors: a meta-analysis
pmc-10566296.creator: Renxian Xie, Hongxin Huang, Tong Chen, Xuehan Huang, Chuangzhen Chen
pmc-10566296.description: Background: Pelareorep is an oncolytic virus that causes oncolytic effects in many solid tumors, and it has shown therapeutic benefits. However, few studies have compared pelareorep combined with chemotherapy to traditional chemotherapy alone in advanced solid tumors. Consequently, we intended to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of pelareorep plus chemotherapy in this paper.

pmc-10648873.title: Quantitative CT at Follow-Up of COVID-19 Pneumonia: Relationship with Pulmonary Function Tests
pmc-10648873.creator: Davide Colombi, Marcello Petrini, Camilla Risoli, Angelo Mangia, Gianluca Milanese, Mario Silva, Cosimo Franco, Nicola Sverzellati, Emanuele Michieletti, Philippe A Grenier
pmc-10648873.description: Background: The role of quantitative chest computed tomography (CT) is controversial in the follow-up of patients with COVID-19 pneumonia. The aim of this study was to test during the follow-up of COVID-19 pneumonia the association between pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and quantitative parameters extrapolated from follow-up (FU) CT scans performed at least 6 months after COVID-19 onset.

pmc-11467598.title: Graded Intensity Aerobic Exercise to Improve Cerebrovascular Function and Performance in Older Veterans: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11467598.creator: Medina Oneyi Bello, Kevin Michael Mammino, Mark Anthony Vernon, Daniel G Wakeman, Chanse Aerius Denmon, Lisa Crystal Krishnamurthy, Venkatagiri Krishnamurthy, Keith Matthew McGregor, Thomas Samuel Novak, Joe Robert Nocera, Amaryllis Mavragani, Edward S S Bliss, Dean E Mills
pmc-11467598.description: BackgroundGrowing health care challenges resulting from a rapidly expanding aging population necessitate examining effective rehabilitation techniques that mitigate age-related comorbidity and improve quality of life. To date, exercise is one of a few proven interventions known to attenuate age-related declines in cognitive and sensorimotor functions critical to sustained independence.

Introduction

Plasma cell dyscrasias (PCD), such as multiple myeloma (MM) and Waldenström macroglobulinemia (WM), are hematologic malignancies characterized by the proliferation of neoplastic plasma cells in the bone marrow that secrete a monoclonal immunoglobulin.

pmc-13540581.creator: Ravi Ramessur, Faradia Kernizan, Ehsan Ranjbar, Nehal N Mehta, Abass Alavi, Daniel B Shin, Gianluca Iacobellis, Joel M Gelfand
pmc-13540581.description: BackgroundPsoriasis is associated with increased epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), a metabolically active fat depot in direct contact with the myocardium, and a mediator of coronary artery disease and atrial fibrillation. The effects of psoriasis treatments on EAT are largely unknown. We conducted a post hoc analysis of the Vascular Inflammation in Psoriasis (VIP) trial (NCT01553058, NCT01866592).

uslaw-usc-t10-s704a.title: 10 U.S.C. § 704a — Administration of leave: prohibition on authorizing, granting, or assigning leave not expressly authorized by law
uslaw-usc-t10-s704a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s704a.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 40 (Leave). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. No member or category of members of the armed forces may be authorized, granted, or assigned leave, including uncharged leave, not expressly authorized by a provision of this chapter or another statute unless expressly authorized by an Act of Congress enacted after the date.
